target_customer: Navies and coastal infrastructure operators in Europe, NATO and allied countries
problem: Naval assets and subsea infrastructure face underwater threats, and current underwater robotics are costly and not built for swarms.
business_model: Defense hardware sales of modular unmanned underwater vehicles; no revenue stated

founders.name: Remi Bouteiller
founders.background_notes: Embedded systems engineer per the company site; YC page calls him a European robotic champion.

competitors.name: Vatn Systems
competitors.what: Modular autonomous underwater vehicles for the US military

competitors.name: Arkeocean
competitors.what: French micro AUV swarms for underwater barriers
competitors.traction_then: 25 platforms in production for a swarm series, French navy sea trials

competitors.name: Anduril
competitors.traction_then: Pentagon selected it to continue production

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwater navigation, perception and swarm coordination with limited connectivity are hard; a first modular prototype was built in a week and tested in water in 2026.

defensibility.rationale: Early prototype with no stated contracts and credible funded rivals; government relationships might build a moat later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Large primes and funded startups were already building underwater drones.

market_need_then: France budgeted 5B euros for drones in its 2024 to 2030 military plan and ordered an unmanned submarine demonstrator from Naval Group, per press found, which signals defense demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses aicepower.com; the YC launch listing used the name AICE Power.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found

rebrands.why: Pivot after talking to submariners, per aggregator profiles; the name AICE Power was kept in the domain and launch title.

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with an aluminium conference, a crypto token and an Asian AI company named AICE, and no brand press was found.

pivots.from: Energy sensors that cut building power bills
pivots.why: Founders spoke with submariners, naval operators and defense engineers and found a gap in underwater systems; dated by an aggregator, not the company.

outcome_analysis: AICE is a two-founder Spring 2026 YC company that pivoted from energy sensors to underwater defense drones and has an in-water prototype. Funding amounts conflict and are unverified, and larger funded rivals exist, so the outcome is not yet determined.
notes: Funding unverified: Yespress says 130K seed via YC in March 2026; FundedIQ says 500K pre-seed in June 2026 and may describe the earlier energy business; no named investors except YC, so no round is recorded. Location conflicts: YC says Paris, other sources say San Francisco or Versailles. The pivot date comes from one aggregator. Outcome search returned only unrelated AICE entities. Completeness pass: Both rounds rest on single outlets (FundedIQ and Yespress) and may describe the same YC investment; amounts and dates conflict and are not summed. CFNews covers Aice Power's seed with no amount in the snippet.
